accuracy_findings.claim: Unique and Limited buildings: "Most buildings can fill every free tile of their body type. Two kinds cannot."
accuracy_findings.problem: Content shows the opposite: most buildings are Unique or Limited. Only a minority have no limit, at every speed.
accuracy_findings.evidence: tmp/help-review/buildings-acc-r0-counts.exs (RC.Help.Data.buildings, biome open/dome/orbital): slow total=45 %{none: 11, unique_body: 26, unique_system: 8}; medium total=45 %{none: 11, unique_body: 26, unique_system: 8}; fast total=33 %{none: 6, unique_body: 19, unique_system: 8}. The compiled {table:buildings_list} agrees: 26 Limited, 8 Unique and 11 with no limit at Legacy. Both infrastructure buildings are Limited too (infra_open and infra_dome limit=:unique_body).
accuracy_findings.fix: Say it without a number, for example: "A building with no limit can fill every free tile of its body type. Most buildings are Unique or Limited instead." Or: "Some buildings can fill every free tile of their body type. Unique and Limited buildings cannot."

accuracy_findings.claim: Where buildings go: "Gas giants and asteroid belts have no tiles."
accuracy_findings.problem: With the frontier mutators, every generated body gets 1 or 2 extra tiles, gas giants and asteroid belts included. Those tiles are never shown (BodiesItem.vue only renders habitable_planet, sterile_planet, moon and asteroid) and take no building (biome :none, so :wrong_biome). So what holds in every game is that they take no buildings, not that they have no tiles.
accuracy_findings.evidence: stellar_body.ex:33 extra_tiles = Instance.Mutators.extra_tiles(instance_id); :53 tile_count = random(gen_tiles_number) + extra_tiles for every body; mutator.ex:902-907 gives sprawling_frontier 2 and open_frontier 1; content gaseous_giant and asteroid_belt have tiles=0..0 and biome=none; BodiesItem.vue:99-104 validBodies.
accuracy_findings.fix: "Gas giants and asteroid belts take no buildings. See [[stellar-bodies]]."

accuracy_findings.claim: Destroying a building: "A building cannot be destroyed while it is being upgraded or repaired."
accuracy_findings.problem: The brief's list is "Not while the tile is being built, upgraded or repaired." The page leaves out a tile still being built. The server refuses Destroy there too, though the UI shows no Destroy button on such a tile, and the player cancels the order instead.
accuracy_findings.evidence: Run: destroy queued (being built) returns {:error, :no_removal_under_construction}, and so do destroy upgrading and destroy while repairing (stellar_system.ex:575). BodiesItem.vue:229-231 offers delete only when construction_status is 'none'.
accuracy_findings.fix: Optional: "A building cannot be destroyed while it is being built, upgraded or repaired." Or keep the sentence as it is, since an order still being built is cancelled rather than destroyed (see [[construction-queue]]).

clarity_findings.claim: "The build menu greys out a building the limit blocks, as it does with box 2 in the picture above." (## Unique and Limited buildings, last line before ## Destroying a building)
clarity_findings.problem: Rule 8 says to show a UI state with {shot:} and a highlight box, "then refer to 'the highlighted readout'." Every other shot reference in the manual (population-status, production, ideology, defense, stability, credit, dominion-tax-rate, technology, system-outputs, self-development, and this same page's foreign-tiles shot) follows that pattern by putting "the highlighted X" inside the caption itself. This is the only place in the manual that instead narrates the mark by number ("box 2") in body prose after the caption, which breaks the established convention.
clarity_findings.fix: Fold the reference into the caption (e.g. extend the build-menu caption to note the greyed card is the one shown), or rephrase in body prose using the page's established pattern: "...as the highlighted card above shows." instead of "as it does with box 2 in the picture above."

clarity_findings.claim: "What you see of the buildings in a system outside your faction depends on your system visibility of it." (## Buildings of other players, opening sentence)
clarity_findings.problem: "your system visibility of it" is a slightly awkward construction for a reader meeting the term "system visibility" for the first time in this sentence; the double possessive ("your ... of it") makes it read less like plain, friendly prose than the rest of the page.
clarity_findings.fix: Rephrase for a smoother first read, e.g. "What you see of another faction's buildings depends on your system visibility of that system." or "...depends on how much system visibility you have of it."

clarity_findings.claim: "Each building's page and the table at the end of this page say which type it fits." (## Where buildings go, closing sentence)
clarity_findings.problem: Two different "page" referents sit close together in one sentence (the building's own catalog page vs. the current Buildings page), which can cause a momentary re-read even though "this page" ultimately disambiguates it.
clarity_findings.fix: Separate the two page references, e.g. "Each building's own page says which type it fits, as does the table at the end of this one."

clarity_findings.claim: Rule 17 ("Every other mechanic named in the prose is a [[link]] the first time it appears") is violated: the damaged-buildings mechanic is named before it is linked.
clarity_findings.problem: In `## Destroying a building` the bullet reads "A damaged building can be destroyed." — this is the first mention of the damaged-building state anywhere on the page, and it carries no link. The link to `[[damaged-buildings]]` only shows up two sentences later, in the following `## Damage` section ("A damaged building gives no bonuses until it is repaired. See [[damaged-buildings]]."). A reader who hits the first mention has no way to jump to the page that explains what "damaged" means. The guide map's own linking plan treats exactly this phrase as linkable (it rewrites the same words on `workforce.md` as `[[damaged-buildings|A damaged building]]`), so this is a same-page inconsistency, not a stylistic choice.
clarity_findings.fix: Link the first occurrence instead of the second, e.g. "A [[damaged-buildings|damaged]] building can be destroyed." in the Destroying section; the later mention in Damage can stay plain text or keep its own "See [[damaged-buildings]]."
clarity_findings.evidence: priv/help/en/buildings/buildings.md, `## Destroying a building` bullet list vs. `## Damage` section; confirmed via the compiled HTML (--live --page buildings), where the Destroying-section bullet has no <a> and the Damage-section sentence does.

clarity_findings.claim: The page's second sentence reads awkwardly for a player-facing tone (rule 1).
clarity_findings.problem: "Every building has its own page, which the ? on its card opens." front-loads a relative clause onto a UI symbol as its grammatical subject, which is a stiffer construction than the rest of the page's short, direct sentences.
clarity_findings.fix: Split it, e.g. "Every building has its own page. Open it from the ? on its card."

clarity_findings.claim: The `## Damage` section spells out the specific list of Navarch actions that damage buildings, duplicating wording that `damaged-buildings.md` owns almost verbatim, instead of using the guide brief's generic phrasing plus a link.
clarity_findings.problem: The page says "When a Navarch's conquest, bombardment or pillage resolves, it can damage buildings. See [[siege]]." The guide map's own brief for this section asks for "a Navarch's attack can damage buildings when it resolves (→ [[siege]] for which ones)" — i.e. keep it generic and let the link answer "which ones." Spelling out the three action types here partially pre-empts what `damaged-buildings.md` (whose OWNS list states almost this exact sentence) and `[[siege]]` are supposed to explain, in the spirit of rule 4 (point instead of half-explaining).
clarity_findings.fix: Use the guide brief's generic wording, e.g. "A Navarch's attack can damage buildings when it resolves. See [[siege]] for which ones.", and leave the specific action list to the linked pages.

clarity_findings.claim: The callback "like the highlighted Limited building above" (in `## Unique and Limited buildings`) is a distant, imprecise reference to the `build-menu` shot shown two headings earlier.
clarity_findings.problem: The shot's marks are labelled locked / disabled / limited / cost, not "a highlighted Limited building" as a single unit, and it appears a full section (Ordering a building) before this callback. A reader re-reading this sentence in isolation has to hunt back and guess which of the four marks is meant.
clarity_findings.fix: Either repeat a small `{shot:build-menu#disabled}` here, or drop the backward reference and just state the rule: "The build menu does not let you order a building the limit blocks."
